acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass talks with producer Alex Blumberg, who explains that he wanted to do this show because of his conflicted relationship with his own testosterone. He tells Ira that the reasons go back to a girl in his 8th-grade homeroom. We also hear from a man who stopped producing testosterone due to a medical treatment, and found his entire personality was altered.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: What’s it like to get injected with testosterone? When Griffin Hansbury transitioned, he got massive shots of it and was surprised at the effect it had on him.
acts.title: Infinite Gent

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: The men and women on staff at This American Life decide to get their testosterone levels tested to see who has the most and least, and whether personality traits actually match hormone levels.

songs.t: What Kind of Man are You

acts.title: Contest-osterone

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
What happens when a man suddenly loses all of his testosterone? We return to Alex Blumberg’s interview from the top of the show with a man who that happened to. He says life without testosterone is life without desire. By that he doesn’t mean sexual desire. He means any desire.
He wrote about his experiences, anonymously, in GQ.
acts.title: Life at Zero

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc:
Novelist Miriam Toews interviews her 15-year-old son, someone at an age when boys experience a jolt of ten or twenty times the testosterone they had as children, about all the things she doesn’t understand about what he’s going through.
Miriam's most recent book is called A Truce That Is Not Peace.
acts.title: Learning to Shut Up
